comment: Single source of truth for the conversation_id prefix that marks a local/cluster message-path eval turn as hermetic (#1909). The Python worker owns it as EVAL_ISOLATE_THREAD_PREFIX in apps/worker/src/curie_worker/binding.py (BindingResolver.boot_env omits CURIE_MEMORY_REF when thread_key starts with this prefix). The Rust CLI owns an independent copy in cli/src/queue.rs and stamps it onto each eval case's conversation_id in cli/src/message.rs::run_eval_turns. The two lanes cannot share code across Python/Rust, so the literal is frozen here: changing one language without this file fails that language's test. Kernel.py is deliberately not in the loop (sacred module): it already passes conversation_id through as thread_key. The prefix is disjoint from Slack thread timestamps (d+.d+) the same way hook: conversation ids are, so a reply never inherits a human thread and ambient agent memory cannot ride in on the normal boot_env path. Both lanes reject unknown top-level keys, so adding a key here without teaching both lanes fails both.
